world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: ACCENT TONIQUE. — L'accent tonique consiste dans un ‘coup de voix’ sans élévation sensible du ton. La syllabe qui le porte est prononcée avec plus d'intensité ou d'effort. Il se trouve ordinairement sur la première syllabe non affectée du signe de brièveté. ACCENT DE HAUTEUR. — L'accent de hauteur consiste dans une élévation du ton, soit sur un mot monosyllabique, soit sur une ou plusieurs syllabes du même mot. Il est indiqué par un accent aigu placé sur la syllabe accentuée.
new_statements.translation: STRESS ACCENT. — The stress accent consists in a 'burst of voice' without appreciable raising of pitch. The syllable that bears it is pronounced with more intensity or effort. It is ordinarily found on the first syllable not marked with the sign of shortness. PITCH ACCENT. — The pitch accent consists in a raising of the tone, either on a monosyllabic word or on one or several syllables of the same word. It is indicated by an acute accent placed on the accented syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Intensity stress ordinarily falls on the word's first syllable, unless that syllable carries the breve (short) mark, in which case it falls on the first non-short syllable; pitch ('accent de hauteur', i.e. tone) is independent of it and may sit on any syllable(s).
new_statements.exceptions: 'ordinairement' (ordinarily); syllables marked short are skipped. No lexical exceptions listed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement in a joint grammar sketch for three lects (Gmbwaga = Ngbaka-Ma'bo/Bwaka, Gbanziri, Monjombo) treated by the author as dialects of one language; pre-phonemic missionary description (Rombi 1994 calls it 'des plus sommaires, sinon des plus naïves'). Modern work (Rombi 1994; Rombi & Thomas 2006 via Boyeldieu 2013) treats Gbanzili as a three-level tone language; no modern stress statement was accessible.
new_statements.identity_note: bura1269 'Buraka' [bkg] is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid: Buraka = Boraka/'Bôlaka, which together with Gbanzili forms Gbanziri-Boraka [gbg], glottocode gban1258 (Boyeldieu 2013: 'deux variantes peu différenciées d'une même langue'). Any catalog entry should be filed under gban1258. The quoted statement (Calloc'h 1911) is a joint description of Gmbwaga (Ngbaka Ma'bo), Gbanziri and Monjombo; his Gbanziri data (= his no. 2) are from the Ubangi river missions, not specifically the Buraka/'Bolaka variety.
